title: Smallpox epidemic in central Mexico, 1520
summary: In 1520 smallpox, introduced by the Spanish and their enslaved companions, spread through central Mexico and into Tenochtitlan, killing very large numbers; it took the life of the new Mexica ruler Cuitlahuac within three months of his enthronement. Chroniclers' counts are exaggerated and no reliable death toll exists.

uncertainty.note: The epidemic began on the Veracruz coast (Cempoala) and reached Tenochtitlan later in 1520; the outbreak continued into 1521.

as_recorded.value: The year 1520 was so traumatic that it passed into history as the year of disease
The first outbreak among the indigenous population occurred at the landing area of Cempoalla

where.modern_name: Tenochtitlan (Mexico City) and the Valley of Mexico; central Mexico
where.historical_name: Mexica (Aztec) Triple Alliance; Mexico-Tenochtitlan, shortly before the Spanish conquest of 1521

importance.justification: A foundational epidemic of the Columbian exchange that weakened the Mexica state and helped the Spanish campaign of 1521.

audience_note: Describes mass death from epidemic disease; chronicles speak of people dying in heaps.

sources.title: 1520: Year of Disease (Colonial Epidemics and Mesoamerican Medicine in Sixteenth-Century Mexico)
sources.publisher: Dumbarton Oaks Research Library and Collection, Harvard University
